justification: Standard: adds an opt-in flag to the commit script and commits a decision script that records review verdicts. Not Minor: the decision script writes verdicts to the production review queue when run with --apply. Not Critical: nothing runs in this change, the flag only skips a fleet-wide nightly sweep, both default to the old behaviour, and the decision script is dry-run by default, backs up before writing and changes only status and reviewer fields on pending rows.

pre_impl.existing_data: Waverley's review queue holds 7,920 pending rows for its staged file v1.2-2026-11-10: 4,645 added, 3,250 removed, 25 changed. Of the 3,250 removed rows, 2,919 still have their exact words printed in the new PDF; 331 do not. A dry run of the decision script on the real queue gave approve 4,482, skip 3,532 and wrote nothing.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The 11 November handoff said about 140 rows were left and the decision script ran; the script had a corrupted line in the unpushed copy (carriage returns inside a string) and the queue is 7,920 rows, not 140. Both were fixed or measured before any use.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: dcp_commit_approved.py already ran council_quote --unchecked fleet-wide on every commit (timeout 3300 s) as a nightly job; this adds a flag to skip it for a one-council commit, which already stores its own words per chapter. The decision script reuses CHAPTER_ROWS_SQL from dcp_approve_proven.
pre_impl.external_source_error: If the PDF cannot be read the decision script raises before writing anything; the commit script's own guards and the per-chapter quote step are unchanged.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A rule is approved whose words are not on its page. The script approves a row only when every cell is printed on its stated page or the page either side, and skips everything else.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The flag stops gating either fleet sweep call, or the per-chapter council words step is placed behind the flag, or the decision script approves a row with a cell not on its page or skips a rule worded with should or is required.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Two deliberate breaks of the flag (ignored at the end of a commit, ignored on an idle night) each failed a test.
falsifiable_check.observed_green: 32 related tests pass. A dry run of the decision script on Waverley's real queue returned approve 4,482 and skip 3,532 and wrote nothing.

functions.name: main --skip-fleet-sweep
functions.input: the commit arguments including the skip flag
functions.output: the same commit with the fleet-wide unchecked quote sweep skipped and a printed line saying so
functions.if_none: without the flag the sweep runs exactly as before

functions.name: decide
functions.input: a queued row's change type, text and its page text
functions.output: approve or skip for that row
functions.if_none: an empty text or a removal is skipped, never approved

functions.name: main --apply
functions.input: the chapter list and the apply flag
functions.output: a backup CSV then status, reviewer and reason on pending rows only

values.read_at: the row's own text against its stated page in the chapter's current PDF

queries.purpose: Pending review rows of the named chapters
queries.where_clause: WHERE status = pending AND council and chapter match AND source_content_hash equals the chapter's current hash

break_it.scenario: The fleet sweep is skipped and a rule is left with no quote verdict.
break_it.what_happens: A rule could stay withheld until the nightly run.
break_it.how: The per-chapter quote step for the committed chapter still runs; only the fleet-wide sweep for other councils is skipped and the nightly job still does it.

break_it.scenario: A table cell is missing from its page.
break_it.what_happens: A rule with a wrong cell would be approved.
break_it.how: A row is approved only when every cell is printed on its stated page or a page either side.

break_it.scenario: A real rule worded with should or is required is skipped.
break_it.what_happens: A real rule would be left out of the published plan.
break_it.how: The decision no longer demands a requirement word; the six measured rows from 11 November are tested.

break_it.scenario: The decision script is run with --apply on the wrong chapter.
break_it.what_happens: Verdicts would be written on rows that were not meant to be touched.
break_it.how: It writes only on pending rows of the named chapters, after a CSV backup of every row, and the rollback restores them to pending.

post_merge.manual_verify: python scripts/dcp_commit_approved.py --help lists --skip-fleet-sweep; a Waverley-only commit with the flag prints that the fleet sweep was skipped.
